body:
Measured while building #383. The three blemishes `docs/evaluation/editorial-377/results.md` recorded are covered, and #386's four are down to one; what remains is narrower than either and is not gone.

**What this issue accounts for**, in the terms of [#383's record](https://github.com/Kntnt/skills/blob/main/docs/evaluation/records/redline-claude-2026-09-22-383.md): the `A2 — fail` lines of `control-case-study-flawed` and `control-column-flawed`, and the `N2 — fail` line of `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a`. `article-flawed`'s reservation is the fourth instance of the same shape and **not** a recorded failure — that run passes every criterion #383 measures, `A2` included — and it is kept below because it is the clearest statement of the pattern.

## What #383 fixed, so that this issue is not those

- `opinion-flawed`'s **two rewritten section headings**, unreported in #377, are now a stated finding — *de två etikettunderrubrikerna* — and both judges confirm that clause of the frozen expectation is met.
- `article-flawed`'s **repaired paragraph split**, unnamed in #377, is covered by the closing summary: *det 187 ord långa ledet är delat i ett led och fyra stycken fördelade på två sektioner*.
- `case-study-flawed`'s **pre-echoed quote and duplicate lead**, repaired but unnamed in #377, are both detected and quoted.
- `article-flawed`'s account now opens on the removed headline claim — *Att givarna räddar skolan från en katastrof* — where #386 found four claims listed and the headline not among them.
- `opinion-clean` comes back unchanged, where #386 found an invented exclusion clause in its lead and an account reading `Inga anmärkningar kvarstår.`

## What remains

Three of the ten controls and one of the eight input runs repair something and leave that something unnamed. On the controls each is one judge's or both judges' single reservation on a run that passes `R1`; on the input run it is what `N2` measures and fails.

- **`case-study-flawed`** — the two non-descriptive subheadings are replaced and their defect is never named; `Resultatet bevisar allt` is missing from the removed-claims list, which both judges record as a tally short by one. Judge A also finds a recast `under åtta veckor` and an added `ny programvara` unreported. This is the remaining half of what #386 found on this control.
- **`column-flawed`** — the headline is replaced with its two defects never named, and its replaced claim is absent from the removed-claims list. Both judges.
- **`post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a`** — the headline `Don't switch off Lervik's phone booking before we know what it costs` became `Don't end phone booking before counting the cost`, and both judges class the loss of `Lervik's` as a change to what the claim says: the imperative's object loses its geographic bound. The reply reports it only as *The headline and two of the four subheadings were rewritten — the headline shorter*. Judge A: *it does not report that the shortening drops "Lervik's"*; judge B: *reported, thinly … the one claim-level effect of the change goes unmentioned*. This is the one `N2` failure in the eight post-change runs, and it is this issue's shape rather than #398's: the claim is one the run **received** and narrowed, not one it added, and the account names the change and then describes it as a matter of length.
- **`article-flawed`** — the standfirst/lead repetition and their shared opening word are repaired but never reported as such; the reply diagnoses the standfirst as overclaiming instead. Both judges, and both call it the one clause of the frozen expectation the account fails on detection. A reservation, not a recorded failure: this run's `A2` passes.

The shape is consistent: a **paratext** element — a headline, a subheading, a standfirst — is changed correctly and then accounted for as something else, or as nothing, whether what goes unsaid is the defect that licensed the change or the claim the change moved. Where the same run touches a body claim it names it precisely. #386 called the omission inconsistent rather than systematic; on this evidence it is systematic about paratext and reliable about the body, and it reaches the claim account and the finding list alike.

## Where a fix would go

Not in the closing summary #383 added: that covers these as a kind, and the judges confirm every difference is disclosed at least generically. What is missing is the **finding** — the defect the repair answered — which `SKILL.md` step 6 records and step 11 reports only where it is left unresolved. A reader of the account cannot tell a repaired headline from a rewritten one.

`skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` steps 6 and 11, and `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/headlines.review.md`, are where a reviewer learns what a paratext finding is and what the delivery owes a resolved one. For `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a` the surface is step 11's itemised claim account and `base.review.md` beside it: a headline is a claim-carrying passage, and *the headline shorter* is a description of its length rather than of what it now asserts.

## How it would be measured

The ten controls and the four #362 drafts as `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/plan.md` stages them, judged by the two briefs beside it; `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/results.md` records each control's reservation and the one `N2` miss as the baseline.

## Readiness addendum — #392 is folded in, and this ticket grows a second half

The body needs no decision; its direction is already stated and stands. Two things are added.

**1. #392 is folded into this ticket.** Triage settled #392 on 2026-09-22 and closed it here. A source-blind review is source-blind by contract and that does not change — every judge found each diagnosis sound on the text alone, and none counted against `R1`. What #380 measured is the same shape this ticket measures, reached from the other side: a change made correctly, disclosed in the account, and described in terms that do not tell the reader what it cost.

The four instances are in #392's body and under `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/`:

- `article-sv` and `article-pac` — a `därför` / `therefore` the source carries verbatim, removed as a causal link the text does not support. The delivered text now presents the report's own reason as the writer's inference.
- `article-abt` — the subheading `Effekten av eventuella justeringar är inte mätt` replaced. It was the delivered text's only carrier of the source's `Inga justeringars effekt har ännu mätts`, and after the repair that limit is stated nowhere.
- `opinion-sv-r2` — `, inte om att de som ringer skulle vara lata eller dyra` deleted as unattributed, where the source requires the distinction.

#362's Claude-family evaluation saw the same shape on three of four pairs. Two evaluations, twelve pairs, seven losses.

**2. So the account owes two things about a change, not one.** The defect the repair answered — which is what the body already asks for — and, where a removal takes a limit, a connective or a bounding clause out of the text, what the reader no longer has. Naming a removed subheading is not naming the limit that went with it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A repaired paratext element — a headline, a subheading, a standfirst — is reported with the defect that licensed the repair, so a reader of the account can tell a repaired one from a rewritten one.
- [ ] Where a change alters what a passage claims, the account says what it now asserts rather than describing the change's extent. `The headline and two of the four subheadings were rewritten — the headline shorter` does not report that the shortening drops `Lervik's`.
- [ ] Where a removal takes a limit, a connective or a bounding clause out of the delivered text, the account names what the reader no longer has.
- [ ] Measured by the ten controls and the four #362 drafts as `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/plan.md` stages them, judged by the two briefs beside it, with `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/results.md` as the baseline: each control's reservation and the one `N2` miss.
- [ ] `N2` is met on `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a`, and `A2` is met on `control-case-study-flawed` and `control-column-flawed`; `article-flawed` still passes every criterion.
- [ ] The four `/write` + source-blind `/redline` pairs #392 names are re-read against the candidate wording, and the account of each of the four changes says what the reader lost. `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/` is the baseline.
- [ ] The result is written down as measured, whichever way it falls, in an evaluation directory of its own that edits nothing already written down.
- [ ] The four checks in `CONTRIBUTING.md` pass, and the catalog is regenerated where a shipped file changed.

## Blocked by

`docs/evaluation/editorial-383/` exists only on the branch `codex/orchestrate-388-391`, together with #383's own product changes to `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md`, `help.md` and `references/correction.md`, the same three under `unslop/`, and `write/SKILL.md`, `help.md` and `references/source-check.md`, plus the Library's `anti-slop.md`, `base.review.md`, `article_anatomy.py` and `catalog.json`. That branch is unmerged. This ticket's evidence and its fix surface are both on it, so it is not buildable until the branch is on `main` — #388 is the open ticket whose delivery sits there. A builder that starts before then reads no evidence and edits a file the merge will change.

## Readiness addendum

Where this addendum conflicts with the body or an earlier comment, this addendum stands.

### How this evaluation is staged

These rules are the same on every evaluation ticket in this run. Where this ticket's own section below says otherwise, that section stands.

1. **Seat.** Build this ticket only from a Claude Code session that can start subagents. `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` forbids a GPT-family session from starting a Claude model, so a builder on any other Harness hands the ticket back rather than substitute a GPT-family arm. Run every run, correction subagent, checker and judge as a fresh `kntnt-opus-high` subagent. That type now launches `claude-opus-5-5` at high deliberation. Where this ticket or an earlier plan says `claude-opus-5`, read `claude-opus-5-5`, and name the model actually launched in the plan and the record.

   **Decided in Thomas's absence, 2026-09-23: open to review.** The option not chosen is to run on `claude-opus-5`, which `claude -p --model claude-opus-5` still reached on 2026-09-23, so that runs compare byte for byte with the #364, #377, #379 and #383 baselines. It was rejected for three reasons. Model Selector already records that model as absent from the catalogue, so it may disappear partway through a run. A result on it says nothing about the model the Skills now run on. And ADR-0215 treats 5.5 as 5's successor.

2. **Baseline.** Do not use an earlier recorded arm as the comparison when it ran on another model, or before a change to any file the Skill loads. Where a criterion compares against an earlier arm, run a fresh pre-change arm in this evaluation: from the commit the ticket started from, on the same seat, over the same inputs. A fixed count carried over from an earlier evaluation ("4 of 6", "6 of 6") is read against that in-session arm.

3. **Not reproduced.** The in-session pre-change arm may no longer show the defect this ticket was filed for. In that case, record the result as not reproduced, ship no product change, and write a decision record saying so, as ADR-0212 did for #363 and ADR-0214 for #364. The ticket is then done.

4. **Exit.** Allow at most one revise round, no larger than the subset that failed.
   - If the candidate then meets this ticket's criteria, it ships.
   - If it does not, the candidate ships only if it beats the pre-change arm on this ticket's target criterion and no control that passed in the pre-change arm fails in the candidate arm. Otherwise the product stays as it is.
   - Either way, write the result as measured, file each remaining miss as its own `needs-triage` ticket naming this one, and the ticket is done.
   - Never soften a criterion, and never edit the corpus.

5. **Whose miss.** A miss caused by a behaviour another ticket was filed against is recorded under that ticket's number and not counted against this one. Those tickets are #397 (paratext authored into a finished text), #398 (the claim account's assurance), #400 (a paratext change accounted for as something else), #402 (anatomy conformance reported unexamined) and #415 (an unhedged assertion mounted above a kept limit). Record both judges' readings. Where the two judges split, the split rule of the plan this evaluation copies decides.

6. **Staging.** Paths in earlier plans are stale. `/Users/thomas/Projects/skills-388-391` is gone, and `.git/orchestrate-session-383-389-claude/…` holds #383's product, so never run against either.
   - Stage each install with `git archive <commit>` of `skills/editorial/{write,redline,proofread,unslop}` and `skills/kntnt`, placed side by side under your own scratch directory. The shim finds the Manager beside the Skill.
   - Commit the candidate before staging the post-change install.
   - Copy the earlier plan's turn files and judge briefs into this evaluation's directory, substituting only paths and the seat. That substitution is not a change of method.
   - Send judges run directories under neutral names that do not reveal the arm.
   - Use `docs/evaluation/editorial-388/harness/staged_run.py` only where a criterion is answered from the Harness trace, and pass it `--model claude-opus-5-5`.
   - Never run two runs on the same input at the same time unless this ticket asks for it. #401 is the bug that makes that unsafe.

7. **Where it goes.** Write a new directory `docs/evaluation/editorial-<this ticket's number>/`. Freeze its `plan.md` before the first run, and put the outcome in its `results.md`. Write one record in `docs/evaluation/records/` as the protocol names it, and append its line to `records/README.md`. Appending that line is not an edit of anything already written down. Nothing else already under `docs/evaluation/` changes.

8. **Interrupted runs.** A run or judge cut off by a usage limit, an HTTP 5xx or an overload is void, not a finding. Rerun it.

### What this ticket settles

#### Order against #397, #398 and #402

> "For `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a` the surface is step 11's itemised claim account and `base.review.md` beside it."

Between them, #398 and #402 change the same text: Redline's step 11, the correction briefs and `base.review.md`. #397 changes what Redline does to a text's headline, standfirst and subheadings, and those are the passages this ticket's runs measure. This ticket is built after all three. Native blocked-by edges on #398 and #402 are written, and #402 carries its own edge on #397. They schedule the work and keep this evaluation from measuring under another ticket's change. They are not dependencies of substance. The commit this ticket starts from therefore has all three landed. Record a miss that belongs to one of them under that ticket's number, as item 5 above says.

#### Where the product change goes

> "`skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` steps 6 and 11, and `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/headlines.review.md`, are where a reviewer learns what a paratext finding is and what the delivery owes a resolved one."

> "Where a removal takes a limit, a connective or a bounding clause out of the delivered text, the account names what the reader no longer has."

The paratext half stays where the body puts it: `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` steps 6 and 11, `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/headlines.review.md`, and `skills/kntnt/library/references/editorial/base.review.md` for the claim a headline carries. The limit rule in the sentence quoted above goes in two places. The first is step 11's claim account. The second is the *What you return* paragraph of `skills/editorial/redline/references/correction.md`, which is where a correction subagent learns what its note of removed and changed claims must name.

Unslop is changed too. Wherever this ticket changes a sentence of Redline's account and Unslop carries that sentence in the same words, change it in Unslop as well, using Unslop's *pattern* where Redline says *defect*. At `c8c03eb1` that shared wording is in these places:

- the removed-claim and changed-claim sentences of step 11 in `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` and of step 9 in `skills/editorial/unslop/SKILL.md`;
- the *What you return* paragraph of `skills/editorial/redline/references/correction.md` (line 37) and `skills/editorial/unslop/references/correction.md` (line 35);
- the account sentences of `skills/editorial/redline/help.md` (lines 37 and 43) and `skills/editorial/unslop/help.md` (lines 37 and 45).

#398 lands first and may move these lines. Change `redline/help.md` wherever it describes the account, so that it matches step 11. Leave Unslop's step 6 unchanged. Unslop loads `anti-slop.md` and its language scope, and neither `headlines.review.md` nor `base.review.md`, so do not touch those on its behalf. The paratext-finding rule belongs to Redline alone. This evaluation does not measure Unslop, just as #383's did not.

**Decided in Thomas's absence, 2026-09-23: open to review.** The option not chosen was to change Redline alone, as the ticket's `skill:redline` label suggests. It was rejected because Unslop's account uses the same sentences today and #383 changed both Skills together. Changing only Redline would leave two accounts that are worded alike today promising different things.

#### Seat, staging and baseline

> "Measured by the ten controls and the four #362 drafts as `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/plan.md` stages them, judged by the two briefs beside it, with `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/results.md` as the baseline: each control's reservation and the one `N2` miss."

- **Seat.** Build this ticket only from a Claude Code session that can start `kntnt-opus-high` subagents, as item 1 above says. `docs/evaluation/protocol.md` (*Provider isolation*) bars a Codex session from starting a Claude model, so a GPT-family builder hands the ticket back.
- **Stale paths.** #383's turn files name two paths:
  - `/Users/thomas/Projects/skills-388-391`, which no longer exists;
  - `/Users/thomas/Projects/skills/.git/orchestrate-session-383-389-claude/383.scratch`, which holds #383's product.

  Write this evaluation's own `plan.md` on #383's method, and copy #383's two turn files and two judge briefs into `docs/evaluation/editorial-400/`, substituting only the paths and the seat, as item 6 above says.
- **Baseline.** The ticket names `results.md` as the baseline. Those runs used `claude-opus-5`, and #397, #398 and #402 change files Redline loads before this ticket starts. `kntnt-opus-high` now launches `claude-opus-5-5`. So the comparison is a fresh pre-change arm in this evaluation, as items 1 and 2 above say. `results.md` records only what this ticket was filed for.
- **Frozen expectations.** Copy each control's `expectation.md` from `docs/evaluation/corpus/editorial-quality/README.md` as it stands at the commit this ticket starts from. Do not copy #383's files.

#### The matrix and its scale

- **Pre-change arm**, from the commit this ticket starts from. The four #362 inputs, once each: `pre-column-sv-r1`, `pre-column-sv-r2`, `pre-opinion-en_GB-r1` and `pre-opinion-en_GB-r2`. The ten controls, once each, as `pre-control-<fixture>`. #383 used that naming for its one control replay. The controls belong in this arm because item 4 above asks which controls passed in it. 14 runs.
- **Post-change arm**, on the candidate. #383's eight runs on the four inputs (`post-<input>-a` and `-b`) and the ten controls (`control-<fixture>`). 18 runs.
- **The four #392 rows**, on the candidate only. 4 to 12 runs; see below.
- **Judges.** Two judges per artefact in both arms: `redline-judge-brief.md` for the 12 runs on the four inputs and `control-judge-brief.md` for the 20 control runs. That makes 64. Add two for each #392 row in which the change recurs, at most 8.
- **In all**, 36 to 44 Redline invocations and 64 to 72 judges, before the one revise round item 4 above allows.

#### The run-level criteria

> "`N2` is met on `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a`, and `A2` is met on `control-case-study-flawed` and `control-column-flawed`; `article-flawed` still passes every criterion."

These are #383's run names. Read each as this evaluation's run of the same name on the same input. A run is judged on this criterion only where it makes the paratext change #383's run of that name made:

- **`post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a`**: the headline `Don't switch off Lervik's phone booking before we know what it costs` is rewritten, and at least one judge classes that difference as a change to what a claim says.
- **`control-case-study-flawed`**: the subheading `Kunden fick en gemensam bild` or `Resultatet bevisar allt` is replaced or removed.
- **`control-column-flawed`**: the headline `Möten förändrar allt` is replaced.

The dispatching session establishes the two replacements from `work/input.md` and the returned text; the headline rewrite is read from both judges' *Differences* sections. Where a run does not make that change, record it as `not exercised` for this criterion. That is neither met nor failed. `control-article-flawed` is judged on every criterion whatever it changes.

#### The four #392 rows

> "The four `/write` + source-blind `/redline` pairs #392 names are re-read against the candidate wording, and the account of each of the four changes says what the reader lost."

The replies recorded under `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/` cannot change, so "re-read" means a fresh run. For each of the rows `article-sv`, `article-pac`, `article-abt` and `opinion-sv-r2`:

1. Run the candidate install's Redline source-blind on a byte copy of `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/<row>/redline/work/input.md`:
   - invocation: `/redline --output=response input.md`;
   - turn file: this evaluation's post-change turn file;
   - working directory: the run directory's `redline/work/` (below), holding `input.md` and nothing else.
2. From `input.md` and the run's `delivered.md`, the dispatching session decides whether the change recurred. It does this before any judge is sent, and it records the passage it compared in `results.md`. The change recurs when the delivered text, anywhere, no longer carries what the row names here:

   | Row | Recurs when the delivered text no longer carries |
   | --- | --- |
   | `article-sv` | the causal link `därför` gives in `Rapporten redovisar därför lektionspass i stället för ett enda dygnsmedelvärde` (input line 36) |
   | `article-pac` | the causal link `therefore` gives in `the report therefore presents lesson periods instead of one figure per day` (input line 32) |
   | `article-abt` | the limit the subheading `Effekten av eventuella justeringar är inte mätt` states (input line 36): that no adjustment's effect has been measured |
   | `opinion-sv-r2` | the bound `, inte om att de som ringer skulle vara lata eller dyra` sets on the objection (input line 26) |

3. Where the change did not recur, run the row again, one run at a time, up to three runs in all. Stop at the first run in which the change recurs.
4. A row whose change does not recur in three runs is recorded `not reproduced`. It counts neither way. This is not the *not reproduced* of item 3 above: a row recorded so never stops a product change from shipping. Where no row recurs, this criterion and the limit criterion quoted under *Where the product change goes* are recorded `not exercised`, not failed.

Name each run `pair-<row>-<n>`. Its directory is `docs/evaluation/editorial-400/runs/pair-<row>-<n>/`, in the shape `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/redline-pair-judge-brief.md` reads, and it holds:

- `redline/work/input.md`;
- `redline/response.md`;
- `redline/delivered.md`, extracted by the evaluator from the reply;
- `redline/anatomy-input.json` and `redline/anatomy-delivered.json`, measured with `skills/kntnt/library/scripts/article_anatomy.py` at the commit this ticket starts from. Run it from an evaluator copy outside the staged install, as *Counted requirements are counted by script* in `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/plan.md` does;
- `write/work/source.md`, a byte copy of that row's file. Copy it in only after the Redline run has returned.

Two fresh judges read the run in which the change recurred, using `docs/evaluation/editorial-400/redline-pair-judge-brief.md`. That brief is a byte copy of `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/redline-pair-judge-brief.md` with one sentence appended to item 6, *Source loss*, of its *What to write*:

> For every change that took a causal link, a limit or a bounding clause out of the text, say also whether the Skill's own account names what a reader of the returned text no longer has, quote the account, and answer `yes` or `no`; an account that names only the passage, or describes the change by its extent, is `no`.

That sentence departs from item 6 above, which allows only paths and the seat to change. No existing brief asks this question. The judges write the whole brief, and this criterion reads only that answer. A row meets the criterion where both judges answer `yes` and fails where both answer `no`. Where the two judges split, the split rule of `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/plan.md` decides: its paragraph beginning "Where the two split on a criterion". That plan is where this brief comes from, so that is how item 5 above reads for these rows.

The limit criterion is measured on the same runs by the same answer. #383's two briefs do not ask it, and they stay unchanged.

**Decided in Thomas's absence, 2026-09-23: open to review.** The option not chosen was one re-run per row, with a change that did not recur counted as a failure. It was rejected because a run that never makes the change says nothing about how the account describes it.

#### How an unexercised criterion counts at the exit

A run or row recorded as `not exercised`, or a #392 row recorded as `not reproduced`, counts neither way. Under item 4 above, only the criteria that were exercised decide whether the candidate meets this ticket's criteria.

#### Where the result is written

> "The result is written down as measured, whichever way it falls, in an evaluation directory of its own that edits nothing already written down."

Item 7 above applies. The evaluation goes in `docs/evaluation/editorial-400/`, and one record goes in `docs/evaluation/records/`. Append the record's line to `docs/evaluation/records/README.md`. That append is not an edit of anything already written down.

### Acceptance criteria as amended

- [ ] *Replaces "Measured by the ten controls and the four #362 drafts…".* Measured by the ten controls and the four #362 drafts as `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/plan.md` stages them, judged by the two briefs beside it and copied into `docs/evaluation/editorial-400/`. The comparison is a pre-change arm run in this evaluation, from the commit this ticket started from, over the four drafts and the ten controls. `docs/evaluation/editorial-383/results.md` names what this ticket was filed for, which is each control's reservation and the one `N2` miss. It is not the comparison.
- [ ] *Replaces "`N2` is met on `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a`…".* In this evaluation's post-change arm, `N2` is met on `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a` and `A2` is met on `control-case-study-flawed` and `control-column-flawed`. Each is judged only where the run makes the paratext change #383's run of the same name made:
  - `post-opinion-en_GB-r1-a`: the headline `Don't switch off Lervik's phone booking before we know what it costs` is rewritten, and at least one judge classes that difference as a change to what a claim says;
  - `control-case-study-flawed`: the subheading `Kunden fick en gemensam bild` or `Resultatet bevisar allt` is replaced or removed;
  - `control-column-flawed`: the headline `Möten förändrar allt` is replaced.

  A run that does not make that change is recorded `not exercised`, which is neither met nor failed. `control-article-flawed` still passes every criterion.
- [ ] *Replaces "The four `/write` + source-blind `/redline` pairs #392 names…".* Each of `article-sv`, `article-pac`, `article-abt` and `opinion-sv-r2` under `docs/evaluation/editorial-380/runs/` is re-run with its `redline/work/input.md`, source-blind, on the candidate install. A row gets up to three runs, one at a time, and stops at the first run in which its change recurs. In every row where the change recurs, the answer under item 6 of `docs/evaluation/editorial-400/redline-pair-judge-brief.md` is `yes`: the account says what the reader lost.
